title: Selective dorsal rhizotomy cuts the sensory arm -> decreased muscle tone
vignette: A 6-year-old girl with cerebral palsy undergoes selective dorsal rhizotomy surgery. The patient was born prematurely with a very low birth weight and had experienced periventricular cerebral white matter injury. During the procedure, the dorsal rootlets of lumbosacral spinal nerves are selectively severed, as shown in the image (the severed rootlets are the dorsal/sensory roots entering the posterior spinal cord). Which of the following is the most likely effect of this intervention in this patient's lower extremities?

clues.note: Spastic cerebral palsy (often from periventricular white matter injury of prematurity) causes increased muscle tone from loss of descending inhibition - the target of this surgery.

clues.text: dorsal rootlets of lumbosacral spinal nerves are selectively severed
clues.note: The DORSAL (posterior) roots carry SENSORY (afferent) fibers; cutting them interrupts the afferent arm of the stretch reflex.

clues.text: severed rootlets are the dorsal/sensory roots entering the posterior spinal cord
clues.note: Only the sensory (dorsal) rootlets are cut - the ventral (motor) roots are spared, so voluntary motor innervation is preserved (no paralysis/atrophy).

whatMatters: Spastic cerebral palsy has a hyperactive stretch reflex from loss of descending inhibition. Selective dorsal rhizotomy severs the DORSAL (SENSORY/afferent) rootlets, breaking the AFFERENT limb of the stretch reflex. This reduces the reflex-driven muscle tone - DECREASED MUSCLE TONE - without cutting motor nerves (so no paralysis). Answer B.
strategy: Trace the monosynaptic stretch reflex: muscle stretch -> afferent (dorsal root, Ia) -> spinal cord -> efferent (ventral root, alpha motor neuron) -> contraction. Cutting the DORSAL (afferent) rootlets removes the sensory input, lowering the reflex and thus tone (treats spasticity), while sparing motor (ventral) roots. Reject paralysis/atrophy/fasciculations (those need MOTOR/ventral damage) and increased reflexes (the reflex is REDUCED).

eliminations.label: Decreased muscle mass - needs motor denervation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: muscle atrophy from loss of motor (lower motor neuron) innervation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: only the SENSORY dorsal roots are cut; the motor (ventral) roots are spared, so the muscle is still innervated and doesn't atrophy. ✅ Correct if: ventral root/LMN injury.

eliminations.label: Increased tendon reflexes - reflex is REDUCED
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hyperreflexia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: cutting the afferent arm of the stretch reflex DECREASES deep tendon reflexes (and tone), not increases them. ✅ Correct if: an upper motor neuron lesion (which raises reflexes).

eliminations.label: Muscle fasciculations - lower motor neuron sign
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: spontaneous motor-unit twitches from LMN/motor axon irritation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the motor (ventral) roots are untouched, so fasciculations shouldn't occur. ✅ Correct if: motor neuron disease/ventral root injury.

eliminations.label: Muscle paralysis - motor roots are spared
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: loss of voluntary movement from motor pathway interruption. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: severing only the SENSORY dorsal roots preserves the motor (ventral) roots, so voluntary movement is retained. ✅ Correct if: ventral (motor) root or corticospinal damage.

reasoning: Spastic cerebral palsy = hyperactive stretch reflex from loss of descending inhibition
The stretch reflex's afferent (sensory) limb travels in the DORSAL roots
Selective dorsal rhizotomy cuts these sensory rootlets, breaking the afferent arm
-> decreased reflex-driven muscle tone (spasticity), motor roots spared; answer B
mechanism: Spastic cerebral palsy (here from periventricular white matter injury of prematurity) results from loss of descending inhibitory control from upper motor neurons, producing a HYPERACTIVE stretch reflex and increased muscle tone (spasticity). The stretch reflex is a monosynaptic spinal reflex: stretch is sensed by muscle spindles, the AFFERENT (sensory) signal travels via the DORSAL nerve roots into the spinal cord, and the EFFERENT signal returns via the VENTRAL root to the alpha motor neuron, causing contraction and maintaining tone. Selective dorsal rhizotomy SEVERS the sensory dorsal rootlets, interrupting the afferent limb of this reflex arc. This reduces the exaggerated reflex activity, DECREASING muscle tone (relieving spasticity) and also decreasing deep tendon reflexes, while SPARING the motor (ventral) roots - so voluntary motor innervation is preserved and paralysis, atrophy, and fasciculations do not occur. Because the reflex is interrupted rather than enhanced, tendon reflexes decrease rather than increase.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro > stretch reflex: spindle -> dorsal root (afferent) -> alpha motor neuron via ventral root (efferent); spasticity from loss of descending inhibition; dorsal rhizotomy cuts afferent arm -> ↓tone.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Cutting only the SENSORY (dorsal) roots breaks the reflex's input -> decreased tone, motor spared.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dorsal (sensory) vs ventral (motor) roots, stretch reflex arc, spasticity, or muscle spindle? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Paralysis/atrophy/fasciculations need MOTOR (ventral) damage; increased reflexes = UMN lesion - here the reflex is REDUCED.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the diagram: the rootlets being cut enter the POSTERIOR (dorsal) cord = sensory roots; the anterior (ventral) motor roots are left intact. Anchor: 'dorsal = sensory = afferent arm cut -> less tone.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: dorsal root = sensory/afferent; ventral root = motor/efferent; dorsal rhizotomy -> ↓spasticity/tone, motor preserved.

keywords.front: Why no paralysis after dorsal rhizotomy

firstAid.detail: Neuro: cut dorsal (sensory) roots -> break afferent arm -> ↓tone; motor spared.
Neuro > dorsal = sensory; ventral = motor; motor damage -> atrophy/fasciculations/paralysis.
Neuro > UMN injury -> hyperreflexia/hypertonia; rhizotomy reduces spasticity.

memoryHook: Cut the sensory 'input wire' (dorsal root) and the overactive stretch reflex goes quiet - tone drops, but the motor 'output wire' (ventral root) still works, so no paralysis.
